overview: Timor-Leste, also called East Timor, is a country in South-East Asia covering the eastern half of the island of Timor. Its capital and largest city is Dili. Timor-Leste was a Portuguese colony for centuries and was occupied by Indonesia from 1975; it became independent in 2002. Tetum and Portuguese are its official languages.

geography.text: Timor-Leste is mountainous, with a range running along the length of the island and narrow coastal plains. The country also includes the enclave of Oecusse, inside Indonesian West Timor, and the small islands of Atauro and Jaco. The seas around Atauro have some of the richest coral reefs in the world.

history.text: Portugal colonised Timor from the 1500s. When Portuguese rule ended in 1975, Indonesia invaded, and the occupation that followed cost the lives of more than 100,000 people. In 1999 the East Timorese voted for independence in a UN-run referendum, and the country became independent in 2002.

events.title: Indonesian invasion
events.text: Indonesia invades days after independence is declared.

events.title: Nobel Peace Prize
events.text: José Ramos-Horta and Bishop Belo share the prize.

events.title: Referendum
events.text: East Timorese vote overwhelmingly for independence.

government.text: Timor-Leste is a semi-presidential republic. The President is elected directly, and parliament chooses the Prime Minister. It became independent in 2002 and joined ASEAN in 2025 as its eleventh member.

economy.text: Oil and gas from the Timor Sea have paid for most of the government's spending through a petroleum fund, but these fields are running out. Coffee is the main export apart from oil. Most people depend on farming.

culture.text: Tetum and Portuguese are official languages. Timorese culture mixes Austronesian, Melanesian and Portuguese influences; it is one of only two mostly Catholic countries in Asia. Tais, hand-woven cloth, is listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Tais
items.text: Hand-woven textiles listed by UNESCO in 2021.

items.title: Cristo Rei
items.text: A giant statue of Jesus overlooking Dili.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Timor-Leste first competed at the Olympics in 2000, under the Olympic flag.

items.text: Timorese athletes competed at the Sydney Olympics.

didYouKnow: Timor-Leste became independent in 2002, making it the first new country of the 21st century.
Timor-Leste joined ASEAN in 2025 as its 11th member.

keyPeople.name: José Ramos-Horta
keyPeople.text: Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1996.
